data.segment_description:
(Studio: Katie Couric)  A government bailout to rescue the nation's financial markets reported; details given about the plan; Stock Market Report.  

(Studio: Anthony Mason)  An extraordinary day on Wall Street as a rescue plan is being formulated featured; details given about the measures to insure money market mutual funds and restrict short selling.  [President BUSH&nbsp- says this is a pivotal day and we must act now.]  Statements from Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Federal Reserve Board chairman Ben Bernanke about the need for a bailout quoted.  [New York University Richard SYLLA†- offers perspective on this financial crisis; states the government is taking off bad debts of financial institutions.]  [PAULSON&nbsp- says we are talking hundreds of billions.]  Examples of other recent bailouts and takeovers and the cost to taxpayers listed.  [University of Maryland school of law Michael GREENBERGER†- says the taxpayer is being asked to write off these losses.]  The question of whether confidence and trust has been restored discussed.  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(Washington: Jim Axelrod)  The reaction in Washington to the rescue plan to get capital flowing again featured; details recalled of the 1980s bailout of failed savings and loans.  [BUSH&nbsp- says urgent legislation is needed as soon as possible.]  [Senator Christopher DODD&nbsp- comments on the plan.]  [University of Maryland economist Peter MORICI&nbsp- explains the essentials of the rescue operation and its dependence on housing prices.]  

(Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(Los Angeles; Ben Tracy)  How Wall Street's woes are weighing on the minds of Main Street examined.  [Investor Martha RODRIGUEZ, WOMAN&nbsp- wonder.]  [In response to three questions {from David Landwehr, Sheila Ellis, Russell Cameron, financial experts David BATE†, Louis BARAJAS†- offer advice to people about their money.]

data.segment_title: Campaign 2008 / Obama vs. McCain / The Economy
data.segment_description: (Studio: Katie Couric)  The views of presidential candidates Senators Barack Obama and John McCain on the economy introduced.   (Minneapolis: Chip Reid)  The McCain plan for the economy examined; details given about a Mortgage and Financial Institutions Trust and new laws and regulations to protect consumers.  [In Wisconsin, McCAIN - promises to end corrupt practices on Wall Street and to act against corporate abuse; criticizes Obama for being in the middle of the Washington culture.]   (Studio: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.   (Miami:  Dean Reynolds)  Obama's view on the financial turmoil examined.  [OBAMA - believes the market will settle down; supports the efforts of Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Federal Reserve Board chairman Ben Bernanke to find a solution; criticizes McCain.]   (Studio: Katie Couric; Austin: Bob Schieffer)  How the economic problems are making it harder for McCain to argue he is the candidate of change, so he has lost his momentum and how both candidates will have to offer an economic plan since the campaign will turn on this issue discussed.

data.segment_description: (Studio: Katie Couric)  The announcement by the SEC of its investigation of possible market manipulation noted.   (Washington: Sharyl Attkisson)  Charges the SEC failed to act while the financial institutions were imploding examined; scenes shown of SEC chairman Chris Cox with President Bush; details given about the role of the SEC, the tenure of Cox's predecessor William Donaldson and the stepping down of chairmen Bradford Cook in 1973 and Harvey Pitt in 2002.  [Senator John McCAIN&nbsp- calls for accountability in Washington.]  [Former SEC attorney Howard SCHIFFMAN†- outlines the SEC responsibility.]  [PITT&nbsp- defends Cox.]

(Studio: Katie Couric)  The absence of cooperation from Alaska Governor Sarah Palin in the abuse of power investigation in her state over the firing of the public safety commissioner reported; scenes shown of Palin and family landing in Florida.
